name: Finite-temperature BTZ transport curve
claim: HYP-2026-006's measured transport time T = 2.250 is the ZERO-TEMPERATURE pure-AdS limit. Wang & He (arXiv:2603.07639, 'Black-Hole Signatures in the Finite-Temperature Critical Ising Chain') show the finite-temperature critical Ising chain maps quantitatively onto a mixed thermal-AdS / BTZ saddle, predicting that (a) antipodal boundary transport time follows a universal temperature-dependent curve reflecting horizon absorption, and (b) the high-temperature relaxation timescale equals the BTZ quasi-normal-mode (QNM) frequency. This hypothesis claims that if we thermalize the boundary state of our MERA (finite inverse-temperature beta, e.g. via a thermofield-double / finite-bond-dimension thermal MERA or imaginary-time-evolved boundary state) and re-measure holographic transport time T(beta), then T(beta) will track the Wang-He predicted BTZ curve: T(beta) -> T_0 = 2.250 as beta -> infinity (recovering HYP-006), and T(beta) will DECREASE monotonically with temperature as 1/beta -> T_BTZ-horizon, with the high-T relaxation rate Gamma(beta) equal to the leading BTZ QNM frequency omega_QNM(beta) = (2*pi/beta) * (n + Delta) for the relevant operator scaling dimension Delta. Critically, this BTZ-QNM relaxation is the SAME decay physics that killed HYP-017 (R1: hologron lifetime << measurement window) -- here it is the TARGET observable, not a contaminant, and is measured directly as a relaxation rate rather than inferred from a quasiparticle that has already decayed.
confidence_rationale: Medium. (1) The source (Wang & He 2603.07639) is by the same authors as the hologron-instability paper and makes three sharp, falsifiable quantitative predictions (T-dependent transport curve, BTZ-QNM relaxation, Hawking-Page entropy-derivative dip), so the theoretical anchor is strong and recent. (2) HYP-006's zero-temperature result (T=2.250) is a SUPPORTED, well-characterized baseline, giving a clean beta -> infinity limit to anchor the curve. (3) Held below high because the test requires a NEW simulation -- constructing a controlled finite-temperature boundary state for the MERA (thermal MERA or thermofield double) is nontrivial and introduces a new approximation (finite bond dimension at finite T) whose systematic error is uncharacterized for this system; and the BTZ-QNM rate prediction depends on correctly identifying the operator Delta that dominates relaxation, which is an assumption that itself needs validation. The internal consistency check (beta -> infinity must reproduce 2.250) is a strong guardrail that justifies medium rather than low.
test_design: NEW simulation required. Steps: (1) Construct a finite-temperature boundary state for the critical-Ising MERA at a ladder of inverse temperatures beta in {infinity (=HYP-006 baseline), large, intermediate, small}. Method: thermofield-double doubling of the boundary, OR imaginary-time evolution exp(-beta H/2)|psi> of the boundary state, at N=16 (matching HYP-006) and N=24 for finite-size control. Local statevector simulation (16-24 qubits) is sufficient -- same scale as HYP-006's TESTABLE_NOW transport runs. (2) For each beta, repeat the HYP-006 transport protocol: inject a boundary perturbation, track boundary spin expectation values vs time, extract transport time T(beta) (peak -> dip -> reappearance) and the high-T relaxation rate Gamma(beta) from the envelope decay. (3) From Wang-He 2603.07639, write the predicted T(beta) horizon-absorption curve and omega_QNM(beta) for the dominant operator (test Delta of the energy/stress operator first). (4) Overlay measured T(beta) vs predicted curve; fit measured Gamma(beta) vs omega_QNM(beta). (5) Independent cross-check: compute the boundary entropy derivative dS/dbeta and look for the predicted Hawking-Page dip.
refutation_criteria: REFUTED if any hold: (a) the beta -> infinity (largest beta) limit does NOT reproduce HYP-006's T = 2.250 within 2% -- this is a self-consistency floor; failure means the thermal-state construction is broken, not that the physics is wrong, and the result is INVALID rather than refuting. (b) With (a) satisfied, T(beta) shows NO systematic monotonic temperature dependence (T(beta) flat within error across the beta ladder), contradicting horizon absorption. (c) T(beta) varies with beta but does NOT follow the Wang-He horizon-absorption functional form (a different monotonic shape fits significantly better, reduced chi^2 ratio > 2). (d) The high-T relaxation rate Gamma(beta) does NOT scale as 2*pi/beta (the universal BTZ-QNM scaling), e.g. Gamma is beta-independent or scales as a different power. (b), (c), or (d) refute the BTZ-saddle interpretation of finite-T MERA transport.
hardware_required: Local statevector simulator (Qiskit Aer / NumPy) at 16-24 qubits, same scale and infrastructure as HYP-006. Local GPU sufficient. No quantum hardware, no cloud cost. Estimated compute: a few hours of local CPU/GPU across the beta ladder x 2 N values.

No blocking issues; the only reason this is NEAR_TERM not NOW is the new (modest) thermal-state-construction code surface plus its uncharacterized truncation error.

SIM-2026-026 RESULT (2026-05-16): REFUTED via criterion (b) -- but the PROTOCOL, not the Wang-He physics. Gate 1 passed: T(beta=100)=2.2500, 0.00% residual. Beta ladder N=16 {100,20,10,5,2,1}: T(beta)=2.2500 at every point, 0.00% variation. Root cause proven analytically: exp(-beta*H/2)|psi_gs>=exp(-beta*E_gs/2)|psi_gs>, which normalizes to |psi_gs> for all beta. The single-copy imaginary-time protocol starting from an energy eigenstate is provably identical to the ground state at every temperature. Verified numerically: overlap |<psi_gs|psi_beta>|=1.000000000 at all tested beta. Energy gap Delta_E=0.1251 at N=16. FEASIBILITY VERDICT UPDATED TO NEEDS_REFINEMENT. Protocol must be replaced by one of: (A) imaginary-time TEBD starting from infinite-T product state |+>^L (correct, accessible at chi~32 with tenpy/ITensor), (B) matrix product thermal state at finite bond dimension, or (C) accept the TFD memory cost at smaller N (e.g., N=8: TFD = 2^16 = trivial). The Wang-He BTZ physics claim is NOT refuted by SIM-2026-026 -- only the protocol is shown to be incapable of testing it. Feasibility analysis error: the mandatory constraint incorrectly proposed single-copy imaginary-time as a workaround for TFD memory. The correct workaround is smaller N with TFD, or imaginary-time TEBD from a product-state starting point.
philosophical_implications: HYP-006 established that information transports along geodesics in a STATIC emergent geometry. This hypothesis asks whether the emergent geometry can also have a HORIZON -- whether heating the boundary CFT literally builds a black hole in the MERA bulk that absorbs transported information at a rate set by its quasi-normal modes. If confirmed, it would be the project's first evidence that the entanglement-built bulk is not merely curved but THERMODYNAMIC: temperature on the boundary creates a horizon in the worldline arena, and the worldline interpretation extends from geodesic propagation to geodesic ABSORPTION. It also reframes the HYP-017 failure constructively: the hologron-decay physics that made HYP-017 unmeasurable on Aquila is, viewed correctly, the BTZ quasi-normal-mode ringdown of an emergent black hole -- a feature to be measured, not a bug to be avoided, provided it is observed as a relaxation rate in a controlled simulation rather than chased through a decayed quasiparticle on noisy hardware.

result_note_2026_05_28: SIM-2026-027 (2026-05-28): VERDICT SUPPORTED_AMPLITUDE via the CORRECTED Thermofield-Double protocol that the SIM-026 root-cause analysis prescribed. The protocol error in SIM-026 (single-copy imaginary-time exp(-betaH/2)|psi_gs> = |psi_gs> for an energy eigenstate) is replaced by a genuine purified thermal state |TFD(beta)> = (1/sqrt Z) sum_n exp(-beta E_n/2)|n>_L|n>_R on a doubled L=8 register (2^16). The physical reduced state rho_phys=Tr_R|TFD><TFD|=exp(-betaH)/Z was verified to machine precision (max err ~1e-16); ground-state population of the physical half drops 1.0 -> 0.016 across the ladder (the single-copy state stayed pinned at 1.0 -- this is the escape from the killer identity, confirmed independently by a 3-agent confirm-phase workflow). PRIMARY observable (extractor-independent, verifier-recommended): transport response amplitude A(beta). RESULT: A(beta) decreases monotonically with temperature, Spearman(beta, A_int)=+1.000, 95% degradation cold->hot, Spearman(N_eff, A_int)=-1.000 (perfect anti-correlation with thermal mixing). This is the Wang-He (2603.07639) horizon-absorption sign and monotonicity, AND -- critically -- the NULL CONTROL SIM-2026-028 rules out the generic-thermal-washout confound that the honest-broker review flagged. SIM-028 ran the IDENTICAL TFD+transport+amplitude pipeline on a non-holographic gapped paramagnet (H = -sum X_j - 0.2 sum Z_jZ_{j+1}) on the same L=8 register and beta ladder. RESULT: after dividing out the generic sqrt(purity) decoherence scaling, the control's washout-normalized amplitude is FLAT (~1.0 across the ladder: its entire amplitude drop IS its purity drop -- pure washout), while the holographic case's washout-normalized amplitude is STRUCTURED (stays suppressed ~0.95 then drops to 0.69), differing from the control by 183%. The holographic transport degrades FASTER than its purity loss alone dictates, tied to the critical gap scale (holo gap 0.125 vs control gap 1.60), whereas the gapped control degrades EXACTLY as washout predicts and no more. So the SIM-027 amplitude degradation contains genuine holographic content beyond generic thermal decoherence. FINITE-SIZE CROSS-CHECK (SIM-2026-028-L10, 2026-05-29): the same null-control comparison rerun at L=10 (doubled register 2^20, 1024 physical states) gives the SAME verdict and the SAME qualitative structure -- the holographic washout-normalized curve is sub-unity (dips to 0.79, monotone, slightly CLEANER than the L=8 0.69 with no spurious wiggle), the control stays flat ~1.0 cold-to-mid, and the holographic gap is unchanged at 0.1253. The candidate-holographic structure is therefore NOT an L=8 few-level artifact; it persists at L=10. (Both sizes share the caveat that the raw washout-normalized 'max gap' -- 183% at L=8, 374% at L=10 -- is INFLATED by the control's hot-end overshoot from sqrt(purity) over-correction on a near-maximally-mixed state, which GROWS with size and so confirms it is an artifact, not signal; cite the holographic sub-unity residual instead.) Discrimination of the precise BTZ functional FORM (vs merely 'beyond washout') still requires the functional-form fit and Gamma-QNM scaling, both currently finite-size limited (the time extractor, not the amplitude observable). CAVEATS (honest scope): (1) the BTZ functional-FORM fit is NOT claimed -- the L=8 time extractor is finite-size limited (cold anchor T=1.30 not 2.25; sparse 256-state spectrum, exactly as the adversarial verifier predicted and independently reproduced). (2) Gamma(beta) QNM scaling untestable (envelope R2<0.3 except one spurious hot point). (3) Spectral-truncation Gate 5 passed perfectly (T_full=T_topK, rel_diff=0.0). (4) The load-bearing amplitude observable has NO beta->infinity self-consistency anchor (Gate 1 validates only the time extractor); its validity rests on the verified TFD construction (gs_pop witness), not on a known-baseline check. NEXT for full SUPPORTED + functional form: N=10/12 TFD cross-check (16/268 MB, local) with the HYP-006-tuned time extractor.
